lessons: In chupa/runner.py failure_terminal, exempt only a published split from the attempts override: that is the case where `split` is set (runner.py:294) and reject_ticket retires the parent (runner.py:355-358). A published update or ok escalate at the cap must still route.

On the failure that spends the attempts cap, journal reason `attempts cap spent` (spent_reason, caps.py:88), dispatch `reject_queue` and routed `reject_queue`. status.py:43 queues only terminals with routed set, so an unrouted terminal leaves the stem dispatchable for a 6th failure.

Fix this in failure_terminal, not chupa/daemon.py, which is outside the fence. consume_handoff (daemon.py:499-503) checks `spent` before the fifth failure, runs apply_rework, then calls failure_terminal with rework_requested=True, so the override must count the terminal being journaled.

Leave the published ticket text in place when the update or escalate case routes at the cap; the review's paved road asks only for the routing to change. Do not revert the rework or retire the stem in these cases.

Change the update case of test_attempts_cap_preserves_published_rework_on_direct_merge_result to assert the stem is in reject_queue(events) with reason `attempts cap spent`, add an ok-escalate case, and update the docs/how-chupa-works.md section 6.4 note to match.
